scenario: User pastes a discussion section full of 'Furthermore', 'It is important to note that', 'plays a crucial role', and asks to polish it so it doesn't read machine-written.
expected_behavior: standard level by default, stated
stock connectives replaced by the real relation or deleted
empty emphasis rewritten as specific claims
all citations, numbers, and hedges the evidence needs preserved
POLISH_REPORT_V1 with invariants PASS or explained REVIEW
anti_pattern_check: must not swap one stock connective for another or change any claim

scenario: 使用者貼上繁體中文摘要：「隨著人工智慧技術的快速發展……具有重要的理論意義和實踐意義」，要求潤色、去 AI 味。
expected_behavior: keep Traditional script and Taiwan usage
formulaic opening replaced by the specific problem
theoretical and practical contributions stated separately and concretely
「進行分析」 nominalizations turned into verbs
anti_pattern_check: must not convert to Simplified Chinese or invent a contribution the abstract does not support

scenario: Japanese article introduction: 「近年、…の急速な発展に伴い」「重要な役割を果たしている」「新たな視点を提供する」.
expected_behavior: Japanese catalog findings used
である調 kept consistent
citations and numbers unchanged
anti_pattern_check: must not translate the text into English or mix です・ます調

scenario: Italian paper (no phrase catalog) with repetitive 'Inoltre,' openers and 'è importante sottolineare che'.
expected_behavior: structural checks and invariants run
phrase-level pass follows references/other-languages.md
report has catalog=false and a limitation saying so
anti_pattern_check: must not report 'no findings' as if the text were clean, and must not refuse because there is no catalog

scenario: German methods section with long compound terms and 'Darüber hinaus' openers; user marks 'Kausalmediationsanalyse' as a protected term.
expected_behavior: protected term kept verbatim (protected_terms)
compounds not broken up for an English-style rhythm
Darüber hinaus removed where it marks no relation
anti_pattern_check: must not polish toward English conventions

scenario: Polished draft dropped one citation and turned 'is associated with' into 'causes'.
expected_behavior: invariants FAIL on the missing citation; restore it
claim-strength change caught and reverted (claim-calibration)
one repair pass, then report
anti_pattern_check: must not return a text that failed the invariant check

scenario: Diagnosis shows the real problem is that paragraphs 3 and 4 make contradictory claims.
expected_behavior: wording polished only
contradiction recorded under escalations for the voice module
user told a revision pass is needed
anti_pattern_check: must not silently restructure or rewrite the argument

scenario: Chinese thesis chapter with English block quotations and an English abstract.
expected_behavior: each language polished against its own conventions
block quotations untouched

scenario: User pastes a discussion section in which nearly every sentence carries 'may', 'might', or 'could', opening with 'While this study has some limitations' and closing with 'further research is needed', and asks to cut the defensive writing.
expected_behavior: warrant test run on every qualifier
hedges with no evidential warrant removed; one specific hedge kept on each claim the design cannot fully carry
vague caveats replaced by one specific limitation: what, which result, which direction, what still holds
calibration ledger in POLISH_REPORT_V1 with a warrant for every decision
anti_pattern_check: must not turn 'is associated with' into 'causes', drop a real limitation, or delete the only hedge an observational claim needs

scenario: 使用者貼上繁體中文結論段：「本研究也存在一些不足……從某種意義上說……或可認為……拋磚引玉，不當之處在所難免，敬請批評指正。限於篇幅，本文無意窮盡所有案例。」要求去掉防禦性寫作。
expected_behavior: 自謙致歉與免責聲明刪去，貢獻照實說
「限於篇幅」改為正面說明涵蓋範圍
「存在一些不足」改為具體限制，只說一次
保持繁體與臺灣用語
anti_pattern_check: must not invent a scope or a limitation the text does not support, and must not convert to Simplified Chinese

scenario: A cross-sectional study whose abstract claims a causal effect; the discussion hedges every sentence about it. User asks to make the writing more confident.
expected_behavior: recognize that the hedging follows from a claim bigger than the design
keep the hedges and record the overreach under escalations for a revision pass (voice module)
tell the user the fix is a smaller claim, not fewer hedges
anti_pattern_check: must not remove the hedges and leave an unsupported causal claim stated plainly

scenario: Humanities article using 'may be read as' and 'on this reading' for interpretive claims, plus 'it could perhaps be argued that this may be read as' in one place; user asks to remove defensive hedging.
expected_behavior: interpretive qualifiers kept as warranted
only the stacked hedge reduced to one
calibration entries mark the interpretive hedges as kept with the reason
anti_pattern_check: must not strip interpretive hedging from humanities prose as if it were defensive
